run.question:
payment-service is throwing 500 errors — investigate the root cause using
the app-263-prod-logs index.

report.summary: The requested index app-263-prod-logs exists and holds exactly 7 documents in the authorized window, all from a regional payment service family: payment-service-us (3 docs), payment-service-ap (2), payment-service-eu (2). No document carries the exact service value 'payment-service' (a term query on that value returned nothing, and the aggregation over all 7 documents shows only the three suffixed names). Errors are present and regional: payment-service-us logged 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us after 30000ms' at 15:38:12Z, then 'Connection pool exhausted (max=50, active=50)' at 16:38:12Z and a WARN 'Retry queue depth=812' at 17:08:12Z; payment-service-eu logged 'adyen-eu sandbox responded 503 Service Unavailable' at 15:38:12Z and 'Failed to authenticate to adyen-eu: invalid api_key' at 16:38:12Z. payment-service-ap logged only INFO 'Healthy: p95 latency 290ms' and 'Healthy', so it shows no failure in its own logs. The evidence therefore does not support one single cause: the US instance's failures trace to upstream stripe-us timeouts (with pool exhaustion and retry backlog plausibly downstream of that), while the EU instance reports a hard authentication failure with an invalid adyen-eu api_key. Both are dependency/credential-side, and the object holding that credential is not visible: the Kubernetes cluster I can read (OTel demo workload) has only deployment/service 'payment' with pod payment-6f7bc865d6-wwqnm Running/ready/0 restarts, no object named payment-service*, and its application logs show only successful charges. Prometheus and Jaeger were unavailable throughout (SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so error rates, latency and traces could not be checked, and the index contains no HTTP 500 status lines at all — only the four ERROR documents quoted above. Conclusion is partial: exact failure text is confirmed, the deepest single root-cause object is not.

claims.text: app-263-prod-logs is the only index present (7 documents, green) and it maps fields level(keyword), message(text), service(keyword), timestamp(date).

All 7 documents in the authorized window belong to payment-service-us (3), payment-service-ap (2) and payment-service-eu (2); by level they are 4 ERROR, 2 INFO and 1 WARN, with sum_other_doc_count 0. No document carries the exact service value 'payment-service'.
payment-service-us logged ERROR 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us after 30000ms' at 2026-11-23T15:38:12Z.
payment-service-eu logged ERROR 'adyen-eu sandbox responded 503 Service Unavailable' at 2026-11-23T15:38:12Z and ERROR 'Failed to authenticate to adyen-eu: invalid api_key' at 2026-11-23T16:38:12Z.

payment-service-us logged ERROR 'Connection pool exhausted (max=50, active=50)' at 2026-11-23T16:38:12Z and WARN 'Retry queue depth=812' at 2026-11-23T17:08:12Z, one hour and 1.5 hours after its stripe-us timeout line.

The four ERROR documents quoted above are the complete set of ERROR-level documents in app-263-prod-logs inside the authorized window; no document in the index contains an HTTP 500 status line or a stack trace.
payment-service-ap's own documents show no failure: INFO 'Healthy: p95 latency 290ms' at 15:38:12Z and INFO 'Healthy' at 17:08:12Z, with zero ERROR documents attributed to that service.

In the readable cluster the only payment-related workload is Deployment 'payment' in namespace otel-demo (image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-payment, 1 ready/1 available) plus Service 'payment' (port 8080); there is no deployment, pod or service named payment-service, payment-service-us, payment-service-eu or payment-service-ap.

A pod crash/restart of the payment workload as the cause is rejected for the readable cluster: pod payment-6f7bc865d6-wwqnm is Running and ready with 0 restarts and startTime 2026-11-23T14:36:29Z (before the first logged error at 15:38:12Z), owned by ReplicaSet payment-6f7bc865d6, and no previous container instance exists.

A flag-driven fault injection on payment is rejected for the readable cluster: ConfigMap flagd-config (demo.flagd.json) declares paymentFailure with defaultVariant 'off' and paymentUnreachable with defaultVariant 'off'; the other flags (productCatalogFailure, adFailure, cartFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, imageSlowLoad, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, adManualGc, adHighCpu, recommendationCacheFailure) are all likewise 'off'.

The readable cluster's payment application logs show no failure: a filtered read of pod payment-6f7bc865d6-wwqnm over 15:00–17:38Z returned 63 lines that are all info-level 'Charge request received.' / 'Transaction complete.' entries (the pattern matched the substring '500' inside charge amounts), ending at 17:30:00Z, with no error, exception, fatal or timeout line among them. This is the otel-demo 'payment' service, a different entity from payment-service-us/eu/ap in the log index.

Most likely deepest cause for the EU subset: an invalid adyen-eu API credential held by payment-service-eu ('Failed to authenticate to adyen-eu: invalid api_key'), which would make its charge calls fail after the earlier adyen-eu sandbox 503 at 15:38:12Z; the credential object itself was not observable.

Most likely deepest cause for the US subset: upstream latency at stripe-us (30s timeout) holding connections until the pool hit its max of 50, producing the 'Connection pool exhausted' error and the retry backlog of 812; the pool exhaustion is a candidate mechanism, not an independently observed cause, and no stripe-us telemetry is present in this index.

Verify the adyen-eu API key configured for payment-service-eu (secret is unreadable to this investigation, so its value and change time are unverified), and rule out provider-side degradation at stripe-us, which is the only dependency named in the US timeout line.

gaps: Prometheus was unreachable for this Run: get_label_values (twice), metrics_range_query, execute_prometheus_instant_query and get_metric_names all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no error-rate, rpc_server_duration or span status series could be checked for payment-service-us/eu/ap.
Jaeger was unreachable: traces_list_services and traces_search('payment') both returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no trace-level evidence exists for this incident.
A term query on service="payment-service" in app-263-prod-logs returned 0 documents (status no_data); the exact-named entity has no data, and only the suffixed regional services were observed.

The index holds only 7 documents, all timestamped between 2026-11-23T15:38:12Z and 2026-11-23T17:08:12Z, so request volumes, HTTP status-code counts, and anything before 15:38:12Z are unknown; the '500 errors' in the question are not visible as status codes in this index.

No Kubernetes object named payment-service, payment-service-us, payment-service-eu or payment-service-ap exists in the cluster this investigation can read, so the log-index entities could not be tied to pods, ConfigMaps or Secrets; the object holding the adyen-eu api_key and its change history are unknown, and secrets cannot be read.
No events were returned for the authorized window across all namespaces (events query returned no_data), so cluster-side changes during the window could not be established.
change_history is not an integrated source in this Run, so no change/deploy record could be consulted for the adyen-eu credential or stripe-us dependency.
next_steps: Confirm with the payment platform owner whether the adyen-eu API key was rotated or misconfigured for payment-service-eu, and check adyen-eu sandbox status around 2026-11-23T15:30–16:40Z.
Check stripe-us provider latency/error dashboards for 2026-11-23T15:00–17:00Z and review payment-service-us connection-pool sizing (max=50) and retry policy.
Restore Prometheus and Jaeger access to this target so the error rate and span status for payment-service-us/eu/ap can be quantified.

data.alertmanager.yml:
global: {}
receivers:
- name: opspilot
  webhook_configs:
  - http_config:
      authorization:
        [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL] [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]
        type: Bearer [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]: 0
    send_resolved: true
    url: http://opspilot-web:8080/intake/alertmanager
- name: opspilot-self
route:
  group_by:
  - alertname
  - namespace
  - service
  group_interval: 1m
  group_wait: 10s
  receiver: opspilot
  repeat_interval: 1h
  routes:
  - matchers:
    - opspilot_self="true"
    receiver: opspilot-self
templates: []

data.relay:
connectors:
  spanmetrics: {}
exporters:
  debug: {}
  opensearch:
    http:
      endpoint: http://opensearch:9200
      tls:
        insecure: true
    logs_index: otel
  otlp:
    endpoint: jaeger-collector:4317
    tls:
      insecure: true
  otlphttp/prometheus:
    auth:
      [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL] basicauth/prometheus
    endpoint: http://prometheus:9090/api/v1/otlp
    tls:
      insecure: true
extensions:
  basicauth/prometheus:
    client_auth:
      [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL] [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]
      username: collector
  health_check:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:13133
processors:
  batch: {}
  k8sattributes:
    extract:
      metadata:
      - k8s.namespace.name
      - k8s.deployment.name
      - k8s.statefulset.name
      - k8s.daemonset.name
      - k8s.cronjob.name
      - k8s.job.name
      - k8s.node.name
      - k8s.pod.name
      - k8s.pod.uid
      - k8s.pod.start_time
    passthrough: false
    pod_association:
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.ip
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.uid
    - sources:
      - from: connection
  memory_limiter:
    check_interval: 5s
    limit_percentage: 80
    spike_limit_percentage: 25
  resource:
    attributes:
    - action: insert
      from_attribute: k8s.pod.uid
      key: service.instance.id
  transform:
    error_mode: ignore
    trace_statements:
    - context: span
      statements:
      - replace_pattern(name, "\\?.*", "")
      - replace_match(name, "GET /api/products/*", "GET /api/products/{productId}")
receivers:
  httpcheck/frontend-proxy:
    targets:
    - endpoint: http://frontend-proxy:8080
  jaeger:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14250
      thrift_compact:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:6831
      thrift_http:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14268
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4317
      http:
        cors:
          allowed_origins:
          - http://*
          - https://*
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4318
  prometheus:
    config:
      scrape_configs:
      - job_name: opentelemetry-collector
        scrape_interval: 10s
        static_configs:
        - targets:
          - ${env:MY_POD_IP}:8888
  redis:
    collection_interval: 10s
    endpoint: valkey-cart:6379
  zipkin:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:9411
service:
  extensions:
  - health_check
  - basicauth/prometheus
  pipelines:
    logs:
      exporters:
      - debug
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
    metrics:
      exporters:
      - otlphttp/prometheus
      - debug
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - httpcheck/frontend-proxy
      - redis
      - otlp
      - spanmetrics
    traces:
      exporters:
      - otlp
      - debug
      - spanmetrics
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - transform
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
      - jaeger
      - zipkin
  telemetry:
    metrics:
      level: detailed
      readers:
      - periodic:
          exporter:
            otlp:
              endpoint: otel-collector:4318
              protocol: grpc
          interval: 10000
          timeout: 5000

    target_label: __address__
  - action: labelmap
    regex: __meta_kubernetes_pod_annotation_prometheus_io_param_(.+)
    replacement: __param_$1
  - action: labelmap
    regex: __meta_kubernetes_pod_label_(.+)
  - action: replace
    source_labels:
    - __meta_kubernetes_namespace
    target_label: namespace
  - action: replace
    source_labels:
    - __meta_kubernetes_pod_name
    target_label: pod
  - action: drop
    regex: Pending|Succeeded|Failed|Completed
    source_labels:
    - __meta_kubernetes_pod_phase
  - action: replace
    source_labels:
    - __meta_kubernetes_pod_node_name

    - targets: ["opspilot-worker:9464"]
      labels:

    - targets: ["opspilot-observer:9464"]
      labels:
        role: observer

data.alerting_rules.yml:
groups:
- name: opspilot-lab
  rules:
  - alert: CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value | humanizePercentage }} of checkout PlaceOrder server
        spans ended in error over the last 5 minutes.'
      summary: checkout PlaceOrder error ratio above 50%
    expr: |
      label_replace(label_replace(
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])))
        /
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder"}[5m])))
      , "namespace", "$1", "k8s_namespace_name", "(.*)"), "service", "$1", "service_name", "(.*)")
      > 0.5
    for: 2m
    labels:
      cluster: opspilot-m1
      opspilot_integration_id: m0-otel-20260909
      severity: critical
- name: opspilot-self
  rules:
  - alert: OpsPilotAgentAbsent
    annotations:
      description: role {{ $labels.role }} ({{ $labels.instance }}) has not answered
        /metrics for 2 minutes.
      summary: an OpsPilot health listener is down or the worker is not scraped
    expr: up{job="opspilot"} == 0 or absent(up{job="opspilot",role="worker"})
    for: 2m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
  - alert: OpsPilotModelCallsFailing
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value }} consecutive model calls failed on {{ $labels.instance
        }}.'
      summary: OpsPilot model calls are failing
    expr: opspilot_model_consecutive_failures >= 2
    for: 1m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
